proof.observed: The note no longer asserts 1 GiB as this deployment's standing budget: the mechanism sentence now reads 'held to its own limit of local ephemeral storage', the heading is 'What the limit charges', the admitted-limit paragraph says 'a container's limit equal to its request', and the one place 1 GiB remains as this pod's figure is attributed to the record and to the pod's age. The memory paragraph now calls the per-role numbers Legion's repository defaults, says an operator's runtime.kubernetes.resources decides what a pod carries, and cites the post-apply reading for this deployment. Checks: go env prints /home/legion/go/pkg/mod and /home/legion/.cache/go-build; the two Secret mounts are 9p ro and refuse a touch while the three tmpfs mounts accept one; golden root.json carries memory request = limit 1Gi/1Gi/6Gi/6Gi/4Gi/1Gi; defaultResources gives every role a 1Gi ephemeral-storage request with 20Gi limits for implementer and tester and 10Gi for architect, planner, reviewer and merger, which is what the admitted-limit paragraph cites; the quoted Kubernetes sentence is verbatim at the cited anchor.

And the note as main carries it names no state home and no memory paragraph at all, so these lists and figures are this change's rather than the old note's.
proof.observations: Two wording points for the reviewer, neither a failure and neither false. (1) The orientation paragraph says 'Read your own container's limits rather than any number here' and then explains that only the sandbox's counter is readable from inside and the per-container limits live in the pod spec a role container cannot read — the instruction is for someone with cluster access, but read literally inside a container it points at /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes, which is the 20.4 GB sandbox figure the paragraph below warns against mistaking for a limit. (2) 'the smallest role's memory budget may be well under a gigabyte' is hedged speculation: the smallest memory value in both Legion's defaults and this deployment's measured pod is 1Gi, and 512Mi appears only in the ephemeral-storage rebalance, not in memory. The earlier wording ('on a 1Gi role that is a smaller budget than the disk it was avoiding') was the measured one.
